title: Kenny Chesney Welcomes Fans Into ‘Silver Sands Marina’ During Intimate Nashville Show: 5 Best Moments
summary: The Country Music Hall of Fame member brought fans into the world of Silver Sands Marina with his show at Nashville's The Pinnacle.
contentText:
Three decades ago, East Tennessee native Kenny Chesney was playing tiny dive bars that dotted Nashville’s downtown, such as the Music City dive bar The Turf, playing his songs for anyone who would listen.

He’s long since ascended to being one of country music’s steadiest hitmakers and stadium headliners, as well as a Country Music Hall of Fame member. But Friday night (Sept. 25), to celebrate the release of his 21st studio album , Silver Sands Marina , Chesney traded stadiums and massive screens for a pop-up show at the intimate, 4,500-capacity venue The Pinnacle, not far from those Broadway bars where he got his start.

Over the course of 22 songs, Chesney sailed through a mix of new songs such “Talkin’ Dirt” and the album’s title track, “Silver Sands Marina,” and drew from his deep well of hits on songs like “Reality,” “I Go Back” and “Living in Fast Forward.” He also offered up “something we haven’t done in years,” playing a hit from 2009 “Ain’t Back Yet,” which he last performed back in 2015.

Outside the venue, fans were already getting into the vibe of the album, thanks to the album-themed outdoor area of The Pinnacle. The area included the pink building featured on the album’s cover, as well as pier carnival games, food trucks, a limited-edition vinyl store and more. Fans who didn’t score tickets to the show also had the opportunity to hear the concert, as it was broadcast live on Chesney’s No Shoes Radio , on SiriusXM’s Channel 59.

Inside the venue, Chesney reflected on his early years in the music industry, telling the crowd, “When I first started in this business, I just wanted like one song on the radio so everybody back home would think I was cool where I could prove ‘em wrong or whatever it was..I thought, ‘If I could just get one song on the radio so me and my buddies could go around the country and play the places that our heroes  played, just one time… this past summer was our 34th trip, so it’s pretty cool.”

Energetic fans were packed into the upper balcony, as well as the floor in front of the main stage and surrounding a thrust stage. Ever mindful of his entire audience in the room, Chesney regularly made the rounds to every side of the room throughout the set, waving and smiling at the crowd.

He closed out the evening with “Just Don’t Happen Twice,” before waving to the crowd and signing shirts, hats and vinyl albums. Returning to center stage, he waved to the crowd and said “Thank you for celebrating with us. We’ll see you next summer!”

And indeed he will — Chesney’s 2027 tour will kick off his Original Vibe Room Tour, featuring Eric Church, Sheryl Crow and Greylan James, in April 2027.
